name: Elemental Unrest
summary: Near the Thendal Standing Stones, lesser wind spirits have grown restless. Their sentient elemental benefactors have departed Zephras Isle, and Rorian the Dayseeker sends you into Thendal Grove to find his apprentice, Yala Windwatcher, and learn what troubles the breeze.

sections.title: A Change in the Wind
sections.body: For generations, powerful wind spirits lived beside the people of Zephras. They were sentient, and they guided and protected the islanders. Now those elemental benefactors have departed, leaving Zephras in lasting imbalance. Without them to tend the air, simple sprites reflect the volatile feelings and forces that linger across the land.

sections.title: The Thendal Standing Stones
sections.body: Northeast of Rorian's post, the air near the ancient Thendal Standing Stones has turned hostile. The lesser wind spirits lack true self-awareness, so they act in reaction, not malice. Rorian sent his apprentice, Yala Windwatcher, to watch their erratic behavior from the grove's edge. She is to discover what unseen tension disturbs them.

faq.q: Why are the wind sprites agitated?
faq.answer: Wind sprites grow turbulent when their surroundings fall out of balance. Unlike the island's former elemental benefactors, they lack true self-awareness and instinctively mirror nearby emotions, intentions, and magical forces.

faq.q: Who are the elemental benefactors Rorian mentions?
faq.answer: The elemental benefactors were sentient, benevolent wind spirits who once lived alongside the people of Zephras. Since they departed, the island has suffered continuous unrest without their steadying influence.

faq.q: Where can I find Yala Windwatcher?
faq.answer: Yala Windwatcher is in Thendal Grove, northeast of Rorian's post, watching the agitated wind sprites near the Thendal Standing Stones.
Rorian the Dayseeker is an elder guide on Zephras Isle. He watches over the island's spiritual balance and studies disturbances among its local elementals.
Speaking with Yala leads into an investigation of what causes the turbulence at the standing stones, beginning with Agitators.
The wind sprites are simple, but their agitation makes them erratic and defensive. They react aggressively to intruders while the disturbance lasts.

angles.text: As a shaman, you can read the wind spirits' reflection of Zephras's emotional climate as a warning of deeper trouble in the land.
As a Skyborne, you depend on Zephras Isle's skies. Since the elemental benefactors departed, those skies have grown unpredictable. Stay vigilant.
